questions.text:
Consider a Boolean expression given by [latex] F(X, Y, Z)=\Sigma(3,5,6,7) [/latex].
Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Minterms 3, 5, 6, 7 = 011, 101, 110, 111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = 1 when at least two inputs are 1 (majority function).

- Maxterms are the remaining combinations: [latex]\Pi(0,1,2,4)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Majority function [latex]=XY+YZ+XZ[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Depends on Y: [latex]F(1,0,0)=0[/latex] but [latex]F(1,1,0)=1[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] so not independent of Y.
- Depends on X: [latex]F(0,1,0)=0[/latex] but [latex]F(1,1,0)=1[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] so not independent of X.

Answer: [latex]F=\Pi(0,1,2,4)[/latex] and [latex]F=XY+YZ+XZ[/latex]

[latex] F(X, Y, Z) [/latex] is independent of input [latex] X [/latex]

questions.text: Consider the circuit shown below where the gates may have propagation delays. Assume that all signal transitions occur instantaneously and that wires have no delays. Which of the following statements about the circuit is/are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
The circuit computes [latex]Y=X\cdot\overline{X}[/latex].

- No delays: [latex]X\cdot\overline{X}=0[/latex] always [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Y is always 0 (option 1 TRUE, option 2 FALSE).
- X goes 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1: the AND gate sees X = 1 immediately, but the NOT output is still 1 until its delay passes. For that short time both inputs are 1, so Y gives a transient 1 (glitch) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- X goes 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0: the direct input becomes 0 immediately, so Y stays 0 no matter what the NOT output does [latex]\text{---}[/latex] no transient, FALSE.

Answer: Y is always 0 with no delays; with delays Y can have a transient 1 after X goes 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: With no propagation delays, the output Y is always logic Zero
With no propagation delays, the output Y is always logic One

With propagation delays, the output Y can have a transient logic One after X
transitions from logic Zero to logic One

With propagation delays, the output Y can have a transient logic Zero after X
transitions from logic One to logic Zero

questions.text: Consider a system that uses 5 bits for representing signed integers in 2's complement format. In this system, two integers [latex]A [/latex] and [latex]B [/latex] are represented as [latex]A=01010 [/latex] and [latex]B=11010 [/latex]. Which one of the following operations will result in either an arithmetic overflow or an arithmetic underflow?
questions.solution:
With 5-bit 2's complement the range is [latex]-16[/latex] to [latex]+15[/latex].

[latex]A=01010=+10[/latex], [latex]B=11010=-6[/latex].

- [latex]A+B=4[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits
- [latex]A-B=10+6=16[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] exceeds +15, overflow
- [latex]B-A=-16[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits (lowest value)
- [latex]2B=-12[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fits

Answer: A [latex]-[/latex] B

questions.text:
Consider the IEEE-754 single precision floating point numbers P=0xC1800000 and Q=0x3F5C2EF4.
Which one of the following corresponds to the product of these numbers (i.e., P x Q), represented in the IEEE-754 single precision format?
questions.solution:
P = 0xC1800000: sign 1, exponent [latex]131\Rightarrow2^4[/latex], mantissa 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]P=-16[/latex].

Multiplying Q by [latex]-16[/latex] keeps Q's mantissa, makes the sign 1, and adds 4 to the exponent.
Q's exponent = 0x7E = 126 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] new exponent 130 = 1000 0010.

Bits: 1 | 1000 0010 | (Q's mantissa) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] first 12 bits 1100 0001 0101 = C15, then the rest of the mantissa C2EF4.

Answer: 0xC15C2EF4

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
A Boolean digital circuit is composed using two 4-input multiplexers (M1 and M2) and one 2-input multiplexer (M3) as shown in the figure. X0-X7 are the inputs of the multiplexers M1 and M2 and could be connected to either 0 or 1. The select lines of the multiplexers are connected to Boolean variables A, B and C as shown.

Which one of the following set of values of (X0, X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6, X7) will realise the Boolean function [latex] \bar{A}+\bar{A}\cdot \bar{C}+A\cdot \bar{B}\cdot C[/latex] ?
questions.solution:
M1 and M2 use selects (A, C), so input index = 2A + C. M3 picks M1 when B = 0 and M2 when B = 1.

Simplify: [latex]F=\bar A+\bar A\bar C+A\bar BC=\bar A+A\bar BC[/latex]

- B = 0 (M1): A = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = 1 (X0 = X1 = 1); A = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = C (X2 = 0, X3 = 1)
- B = 1 (M2): A = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = 1 (X4 = X5 = 1); A = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] F = 0 (X6 = X7 = 0)

Answer: (1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0)
